intro.data: A payment is either a card or cash. The tray holds two handlers; bring the right one onto the board and wire the payment to its receipt — it must charge the card AND log the cash. One handler covers both cases; the other mishandles the card. Leave the bad one in the tray.
intro.alchemy: A reagent is either acid or base. The tray holds two handlers; bring the right one onto the board and wire the reagent to its result — it must neutralize both. One covers both cases; the other mishandles one. Leave the bad one in the tray.
intro.spellcraft: A charm is either ward or hex. The tray holds two handlers; bring the right one onto the board and wire the charm to its effect — it must resolve both. One covers both; the other mishandles one. Leave the bad one in the tray.
intro.abstract: ι₁ a tags a as the left option, ι₂ b tags b as the right; [f,g] picks the matching branch for each. From the tray bring the genuine case-split and wire A+B to Y, so ι₁ 3 ↦ 30 and ι₂ 4 ↦ 40; leave the impostor (wrong on the left case) in the tray.

goal.data: Bring the right handler from the tray and wire the payment to its receipt — card AND cash.
goal.alchemy: Bring the right handler from the tray and wire the reagent to its result — acid AND base.
goal.spellcraft: Bring the right handler from the tray and wire the charm to its effect — ward AND hex.
goal.abstract: Bring [f,g] from the tray and wire A+B to Y, handling both injected cases.

afterSuccess.data: Your handler turned a card into its receipt AND a cash payment into its receipt — both cases, one machine. The look-alike mishandled the card. A coproduct's case-split must cover every injection.
afterSuccess.alchemy: Your handler neutralized both acid and base. The look-alike botched one. A case-split must cover every injection.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: Your handler resolved both ward and hex. The look-alike botched one. A case-split must cover every injection.
afterSuccess.abstract: Both injected cases handled: [f,g]∘ι₁ = f and [f,g]∘ι₂ = g. The look-alike failed one case.

reveal.summary: The coproduct is the dual of the product: for f : A→Y and g : B→Y there is a unique [f,g] : A+B→Y with [f,g]∘ι₁ = f and [f,g]∘ι₂ = g — it must handle BOTH cases.
reveal.moreFormal: Reverse every arrow in the product's universal property and you get the coproduct's. Products are 'and'; coproducts are 'or'.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: match (p) { case Card: f(p); case Cash: g(p) } — miss a case and it's wrong.
